'''Nandi Olive Leslie''' is an [[applied mathematician]] and senior engineering fellow at [[Raytheon Technologies]].

== Early life and education ==
'''Leslie''' grew up in [[Evanston, Illinois]] where her father, Joshua Leslie, was a professor of mathematics at [[Northwestern University]]. She enrolled in university math programs at Northwestern and would accompany her father to various math conferences and speeches around the United States.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=February 24, 2021 |title=A mathematician from the start |url=https://www.raytheonintelligenceandspace.com/news/2021/02/24/mathematician-start |access-date= |website=Raytheon Intelligence & Space}}</ref>

Leslie graduated ''[[magna cum laude]]'' with a B.S. in Mathematics from [[Howard University]]<ref name=":2" /> and then a M.A.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nandi Leslie, Mathematician of the African Diaspora |url=http://math.buffalo.edu/mad/PEEPS2/leslie_nandi.html |access-date=2023-04-14 |website=math.buffalo.edu}}</ref> and PhD in Applied and Computational Mathematics and Ecology and Evolutionary Biology from [[Princeton University]]. Her thesis at Princeton was ''Spatial Stochastic Models for Forest Degradation and Deforestation in [[Bolivia]] and Brazil''.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=76372}}</ref>

== Professional career ==
Leslie serves as a Senior Engineering Fellow at [[Raytheon Technologies]] and currently serves as the Raytheon Intelligence and Space Internal Research Development Chief Engineer and Chief [[Data scientist]]. Her research interests include [[machine learning]], stochastic processes, [[cybersecurity]], and sensor performance.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Nandi Olive Leslie, Ph.D. |url=https://csit.udc.edu/mudl/materials/NandiLeslieBIO.pdf}}</ref> In 2019, Leslie became the first African American woman at Raytheon to achieve the distinction of engineering fellow.<ref name=":0" /> She currently serves on five different scientific advisory boards and was received the Black Engineer of the Year Award for Outstanding Technical Contribution in Industry in 2020.<ref name=":2" />

Beginning in 2020, Leslie has served as a Lecturer and Research Advisor for Master's Degree Theses and Computational Mathematics and Data Science Programs at [[Johns Hopkins University]].<ref name=":2" />
